title: Smith Machine Row
summary: A bent-over row on a fixed bar path for the lats and upper back.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for upper back (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.8 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.5 for rear delts (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.
Library rating 0.5 for traps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.5 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly biceps total.
Library rating 0.3 for lower back (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly lower back total.

setup.text: Set the bar at about knee height and grip just outside your legs.
Hinge forward until your torso is about 45 degrees or lower.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs, leading with your elbows.
Lower under control without letting your back round.

form_cues.cue: Pull the bar to your lower ribs
Pause with the bar touching your body to stop momentum taking over.

mistakes.text: Standing more upright with each rep.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Set safety arms or pins where you can fail a rep safely, or use a spotter, and use collars.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: More stretch emphasis, Less upper-back focus, Less spinal loading.
